key_insight: Flexible modular robots combine movement and object handling in a single unit, then physically connect into task-adaptive forms. By changing their collective shape, they can cooperate to carry objects, cross gaps and navigate difficult terrain.
problem_solved: Robots with fixed shapes can struggle when tasks require different physical capabilities. This work addresses the need for robotic units that can both act independently and join together in configurations suited to the task.
method: Use flexible, tensegrity-based continuum robot modules that support both locomotion and manipulation.
Physically connect modules to form cooperative structures adapted to different tasks.
Demonstrate collective capabilities through object transport, gap crossing and challenging-terrain navigation.
impact: For AI and robotics practitioners, this work highlights physical reconfiguration as an additional tool for solving tasks—not just changing a robot's actions. It motivates planning and coordination methods that consider both individual behaviour and collective body shape.
visual_elements: Annotated robot module showing its flexible tensegrity structure and movement capabilities.
Sequence diagram showing separate modules connecting into a task-adaptive formation.
Three-panel illustration of cooperative object carrying, gap crossing and terrain navigation.
Task-to-configuration map linking each challenge to a suitable collective shape.
paper_title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
paper_authors: Mahmud Hasan Saikot, Sydney Spiegel, Sudheera Akalanka Kariyawasam, Andrew Stefka, Josh Chrisler
